sections.title: About NCC
sections.content: Home About NCC About NCC National Cadet Corps MOTO OF NCC : UNITY AND DISCIPLINE 1(T) NAVAL UNIT, SECUNDERABAD GROUP, TROOP NO: 03, INSTITUTION & ANO CODE-TS11802 Admissions Events NCC Manual NCC Magazine Contact Us National Cadet Corps Act of 1948. It was raised on 15 July 1948 The National Cadet Corps T he NCC in India was formed with the National Cadet Corps Act of 1948. It was raised on 15 July 1948 The National Cadet Corps can be considered as a successor of the University Officers Training Corps (UOTC) which was established by the British in 1942. During World War II, the UOTC never came up to the expectations set by the British. This led to the idea that some better schemes should be formed, which could train more young men in a better way, even during peace times. A committee headed by Pandit H.N. Kunzru recommended a cadet organization to be established in schools and colleges at a national level. BACKGROUND: As you are fully aware that NCC plays a vital role in the growth and development of the country by grooming its most precious resource, youth. In order to attain our national goals it is imperative that our training encapsulates and embeds the qualities and attributes in the cadets. Apart from grooming and preparing the youth for the future challenges in NCC, cadets also get various benefits in terms of job opportunities , scholarships and financial assistance in times of any tragedy while undergoing any NCC related activity. INCENTIVES FROM THE CENTRE AND STATE GOVTS ADMISSION IN PRESTIGIOUS EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTES Many educational institutes have seats reserved for the certificate holders from NOC Preference is given in following fields (a) Degree and Diploma courses (b) LLB courses (c) Govt. Polytechnics and Engineering colleges (d) Medical courses RESERVED VACANCIES IN EMPLOYMENT CENTRAL GOVERNMENT JOBS: Specific vacancies in the Armed Forces via-Army, Air Force and Navy are reserved for NCC C Certificate holder candidates. Students opting for Officer Entry through UPS Care exempted from appearing in written examination and have the opportunity to appear directly at Interview by Service Selection Boards, (558) which is an important incentive as normal students have to toil hard in clearing written examination considering the standard of any UPSC exam. The other various incentives for NCC Certificate holders are as enumerated below. (i) Bonus marks are awarded in employment in Para Military Forces and Department of Telecommunication (ii) Can apply for gazetted post in CRPF if cadet holds third division degree in certificate examinations (iii) Employment within NCC Organization as Whole Time Lady Officer, (WTLO) Girl Cadet Instructor, various Instructor post such as Aero and Ship Modeling Instructor etc. STATE GOVERNMENT JOBS: Various states Government provide job incentive to the NCC ‘B’/’C’ certificate holders for recruitment in following departments: (a) Police Services. (b) Transport Department (c) Forest Department. (d) Excise Department. (d) Preference to the girl cadets as nurses, receptionists and telephone operators in various state Government sectors as well as private sector. For More Details Click on Download Download

sections.title: Mandatory Disclosures
sections.content: Sir/Madam, This has a reference to APH Clause 7.38 wherein Mandatory Disclosures as per Annexure – 10 shall be displayed in the website of each Technical Institute. Display of information submitted to AICTE (including the accreditation status and Board of Governors) along with mandatory disclosures in the Website of the Institution is essential as per APH 2020-21. This Office has randomly checked for the same and found Mandatory Disclosure of Old Version or not able to trace on the website of the various institutions. Hence, this is to inform all Technical Institutions under SCRO Hyderabad to adhere with the norms & regulations of the AICTE and the compliance may be reverted back within 10 days. 2025-2026 View 2024-2025 View 2023-2024 View 2022-2023 View 2021-2022 View 2020-2021 View 2019-2020 View 2018-2019 View 2017-2018 View 2016-2017 View 2015-2016 View 2014-2015 View 2013-2014 View 2012-2013 View 2011-2012 View 2010-2011 View 2009-2010 View 2008-2009 View 2007-2008 View 2006-2007 View 2005-2006 View 2004-2005 View 2003-2004 View 2002-2003 View Letter of Intent FROM AICTE View LOI Establishment of Institutions View Autonomous Approval UGC View Autonomous Conferment Letter – JNTUH View HIGHER EDUCATION(TE)DEPARTMENT – 2015 View HIGHER EDUCATION(TE)DEPARTMENT – 2013 View HIGHER EDUCATION(TE)DEPARTMENT – 2012 View HIGHER EDUCATION(TE)DEPARTMENT – 2011 View Affiliation View

sections.content: We are proud to announce that TKR College of Engineering & Technology (TKRCET) has officially established its IEEE Student Branch, recognized by the IEEE Member and Geographic Activities Board under Region 10 (Asia-Pacific) and the Hyderabad Section. The Student Branch (Code: STB60030787, School Code: 60226110) provides a dynamic platform for students to explore innovation, research, leadership, and professional growth in engineering and technology. Through this initiative, TKRCET students gain access to IEEE’s global community, international conferences, technical resources, workshops, research publications, and opportunities to collaborate with industry and academia.

sections.title: IEEE-PELS
sections.content: IEEE-PELS Home IEEE-PELS IEEE-PELS About Members Events TKRCET IEEE PELS SOCIETY About IEEE PELS Student Branch Chapter – TKRCET The IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Student Branch Chapter at TKR College of Engineering & Technology (TKRCET) was officially approved on 2 June 2025, under the IEEE Member and Geographic Activities Board. This chapter is a specialized extension of the IEEE Student Branch (Code: STB60030787, School Code: 60226110) and functions within Region 10 (Asia-Pacific) and the Hyderabad Section. Formation Details Chapter Name : IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Student Branch Chapter, TKRCET Effective Formation Date : 02 June 2025 Approval Authority : IEEE Member and Geographic Activities Board Chapter Advisor : Mr. E. Anjaiah, Assistant Professor, EEE Department Scope and Focus The PELS Chapter is dedicated to advancing knowledge, research, and practical skills in: Power Electronics – conversion systems, semiconductor devices, and energy-efficient technologies. Renewable Energy Integration – solar, wind, hybrid power, and smart storage solutions. Electric Mobility – EV powertrains, charging systems, and advanced battery management. Smart Grids and Automation – modern power systems and intelligent control for sustainable energy. Objectives The IEEE PELS Student Chapter at TKRCET empowers students to: Strengthen technical competence through hands-on projects, workshops, and expert talks. Promote research and innovation in renewable energy and electric mobility. Build strong industry-academia collaboration for career readiness and applied learning. Enhance professional and leadership skills such as teamwork, project management, and entrepreneurship. Uphold ethical and social responsibility while striving for global recognition in IEEE activities.

sections.title: IV. Governance.
sections.content:
Members of the Board and their brief background. 
(a). Shri Teegala Krishna Reddy is the founder chairperson of TKRES. 
A Philanthropist by nature. His urge to see our students excelling themselves in all fields , 
prompted him to start the Educational Society, making it easy for education to be within arms’ 
length of even a rural student and providing them with an independent and easy track for pursuing 
their dreams and making them come true and in the process, upholding moral and ethical values. 
(b). Smt. Teegala Arundhati Reddy is the Vice-Chairperson of TKRES. She takes an active 
interest in the curricular activities of the college and her encouragement and co-operation is 
always for the betterment of the students and furthering their career prospects and for the 
developmental activities undertaken by the college.   
(c). The person who puts in all his efforts to see the students excelling themselves and takes great 
pride in watching them carve out a niche for themselves is none other than Dr. Teegala Harinath 
Reddy, the Secretary of the college. A calm and serene countenance with sharp, twinkling eyes, 
he is the pivotal of encouragement and is always on the look-out for avenues which would 
provide the wherewithal for developing a cutting edge to their capabilities and potentialities. 
(d). Smt. Teegala Tulasi Reddy is the Joint-Secretary of the college. Being an extrovert, she has 
a very good rapport with the students during her visits to the college and her amiable nature 
helps her in getting the pulse of the students.

the students’ overall personality and his financial back-up for any activities is confirmed

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: The guidelines published in this document are for the Governance of T.K.R. College of Engineering & Technology (TKRCET), sponsored by T.K.R. Educational Society, (TKRES), Hyderabad, Telangana. The document is a fusion product based on a. The University Grants Commission, New Delhi, India guidelines for autonomous colleges. b. Bye laws of T.K.R Educational Society, Hyderabad, Telanagna. c. Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University rules and regulation for affiliated colleges d. Previous documents viz Administrative manual of the college e. Existing Best Practices in the institution. The Good Governance Guidelines Document has been prepared to ensure an effective functioning and efficient governance at all levels to the satisfaction of stakeholders. This document provides core principles of good governance. The implementation of these governance guidelines shall lead to effective utilization of manpower, infrastructure and facilities available in the institute and thereby enhance the quality of education. The guidelines will lead to transparency and accountability in the administration. The expected benefits due to implementation of good governance through the guidelines presented in the document may include:  To strengthen the existing good practices.  To implement transparency at all levels of governance and administration.  To follow integrity in appointments at all levels.  To strengthen the Industry-Institute interaction.  To establish fair and transparent processes in internal control.  To comply with rules and regulations.  To establish strong and capable financial processes and procedures relating to procurement, appropriate utilization of funds and audit.  To, involve all the stake holders at various levels as deemed fit with regard to guidelines of statutory bodies.  To maintain registry of interests of members of governing body.  To achieve optimum utilization of infrastructure, resources for better output.  To establish processes in risk management. 2  To meet the requirements of accreditations.  To enhance the quality of teaching-learning process.  To set up more centers of excellence in research & development and enhancement of quality of research and consultancy.  To set up and strengthen student support programs, training for enhancing quality in placements and higher education.  To place improved systems for feedback, self-appraisal of faculty and staff.  To create bench marking with other institutes of repute.  To accomplish appraisal of Head of the Institution. The document provides information on organization of the institute along with its organization structure, functions, and responsibilities of all four statutory bodies namely Board of Governors (BoG), Academic Council, BOS and Finance Committee as per the UGC guidelines for autonomous colleges. In addition, it outlines the responsibilities of various functionaries in the academics and administration including non-saturatory committees formed for the smooth and effective functioning of the college. The Good Governance Document can be appended subject to approval of BoG Members and if any ambiguity occurs in the process the Affiliating University Guidelines will be followed.

sections.title: Preamble
sections.content: I. The regulations stated herein below shall be called the T.K.R. College of Engineering & Technology “Good Governance Guidelines Document”. II. These regulations shall be in force from the academic year 20117-2018 by the date of approval by the Governing Body of the college. III. In the event of any doubt about the interpretation of these regulations, the matter shall be referred to the Governing Body and its decision shall be final. IV. The Governing Body shall have the authority to modify, amend and repeal any of the provisions of these regulations.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.content: In this document, unless there is anything repugnant to the subject or context I. “College” means “T.K.R. College of Engineering & Technology”, Meerpet, Hyderabad. II. “Student” means a candidate who has taken admission into B.Tech / M.Tech / MBA course of this college as per the guidelines stipulated from time to time by the Government of Telangana for admissions into various courses of study and the affiliating university, Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Hyderabad. III. “Government” means the Government of Telangana. IV. “Board of Governors” means the members of Governing Body constituted as per the guidelines of UGC. V. “Academic Council” means the Academic council constituted as per the guidelines of UGC. VI. “Board of Studies” means Board of Studies constituted in each department as per the guidelines of UGC VII. “Finance Committee” means the committee constituted as per the guidelines of UGC to look into financial aspects of the institution. VIII. “Chairman” means chairman of the Board of Governors of T.K.R. College of Engineering & Technology. IX. “President” means the President of T.K.R Educational Society, Hyderabad. X. “Secretary” means the Secretary of T.K.R Educational Society, Hyderabad. XI. “Principal” means the Head of the institution XII. “Controller of Examinations” means the Controller of Examinations of the College XIII. “Head of the Department” means the Head of an Academic Department of the College. XIV. “Faculty member” means the teacher (Assistant/Associate/Professor) working on regular or Adhoc basis in any of the Academic Departments of the College.

sections.title: Brief Profile of Institution
sections.content: TKR College of Engineering & Technology, established in the year 2002, has been sponsored by TKR Educational Society, Medbowli, Meerpet, Hyderabad, Telangana. It is recognized by AICTE and approved by the State Govt. now Telangana, permanently affiliated to Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH). UGC recognition under Sections 2(f) and 12 (B) further strengthens over cause of quality education. This Professional college has been established with a cherished vision to provide quality education and to be among the best of the institutions for the budding engineers and technologists. With added emphasis on attitudes, skills and knowledge it has become the epicenter of creative solutions to scores of students from varied backgrounds. The College proudly offers 6 UG and 3 PG programmes in Engineering, a Professional Course in MBA and 5 programmes in Diploma Course. With 15years of rich standing in the educational era, TKR College of Engineering & Technology has an excellent track record which is evidenced across holding accreditation by NBA in 2008 for 3 years and Re-accreditation for 2 years in 2015, and subsequently extended for one more year. This Institution has the distinction of being one among the Top 10 Ranking and Reckoning Institutes of choice and preference for the aspiring students.

sections.title: VISION, MISSION, QUALITY POLICY, AND POLICY STATEMENT
sections.content: VISION: The Institution endeavors towards imparting quality education with ethical values and strives to make students technically competent to reach heights and make our nation self-reliant and globally recognized. MISSION: The Institution is committed and dedicated to mould the students into quality Engineers and technologists with aplomb by providing world-class scientific and technical education through:  Ensuring excellent branch wise Infrastructural facilities, with eminent and qualified faculty.  Making the Institute a research/resource center to enhance scope for consultancy, Research & Development. QUALITY POLICY: The Institute encourages continuous improvement and innovation at various levels for developing the institute into a center of excellence, thus satisfying the aspiration of all stakeholders. POLICY STATEMENT: We are committed towards developing and advancing the college as an institution of higher learning by offering quality education through excellent infrastructure, quality teaching learning process and congenial ambience. The innate talents of students are nurtured through overall development by providing a number of curricular, co-curricular and extracurricular activities. We are also committed to implementing effective and transparent appraisal system. A good exposure to the students will be offered through enhanced industry- institution interaction, MOUs, expert lecturers, entrepreneurship, research and consultancy. The college provides conducive work environment to the faculty and staff by offering best facilities and salaries as per the UGC guidelines for knowledge update, qualification improvement, etc.

sections.title: STRATEGIC PLAN & PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT DOCUMENT
sections.content:
1. Understand education policies and defined structure of engineering education to raise the standards. 
 To define the Vision and Mission of the department in line to Vision and Mission of Institute. 
 To enmark long, term goals and short term goals precisely. 
 Establish a monitoring committee and frame work for validating the methods and process for achieving long and short-term goals.

sections.title: 2. To establish Department Academic Committee and perform the tasks based on the objectives for improving the quality.
sections.content:
The Department Academic Committee (DAC) acts as an advisory committee responsible for all matters related to academics of the department. The committee exercises its functionality by demonstrating polices framed by the academic council. The objectives of DAC is given below, 

DAC OBJECTIVES 
 Prepare a plan of action for implementing academic activity involving all stakeholders. 
 To Exercise the needs of industry from the feedbacks of campus hiring organizations. 
 Based on the needs to establish portfolios. 
 To suggest Board of Studies for incorporating the same in the design and development of curriculum. 
 To define policies based on the needs of industry (MoUs), learning (bridging gaps). Plan of action (time tables/activity chart). 
 To identify gaps and bridge the gaps among student community based on their learning ability. 
 To exercise the scope of improvements in teaching and research achievements, projects, awards and co-curricular activities required for students. 
 To ensure that the academic activities are planned in a way to achieve PSO’s and CO’s.

sections.title: 3. To map the curriculum with industrial needs through defining Course outcomes and programme specific outcomes.
sections.content:
 To Design the structure of curriculum in line to define polices by the institute. 
 To gather feedback from all the stakeholders involved in framing the guidelines for programme development. 
 To evolve a strategic plan for quality output, continuous improvement. 
 To impart plan of action for diversified learning student community. 
 To formulate the content based on 1 to 4. 
 To draft the outcomes and objectives of a course in line to standard metric (Blooms Taxonomy).

sections.title: 4. Propose methods for imparting knowledge. To adapt methodologies for self-learning.
sections.content:
 To prepare a detailed course hand out. 
 To plan the necessary schedule for delivering lectures, to achieve course outcomes. 
 To follow the IQAC guidelines (pre, post reviews of teaching methodologies). 
 To engage and motivate in e-based learning using various available resources. 
 To map the learned outcomes with programme outcomes (defined polices by DAC). 
 To plan for imparting the content designed by BOS for diversified student-learning community. 
Incorporate the mechanism of imparting knowledge to develop, logic, reasoning, and vocabulary as a part of skill development.

sections.title: 5. Plan assessments to test the gained knowledge of students and identify the gaps in gaining the knowledge.
sections.content:
 To elaborate a detailed process of assessment. 
 To formulate questions to assess the knowledge gained in line to course outcomes. 
 To state different levels for grading the student community, to create a scope of improvements if any. 
 To articulate the assessment framework inline to defined course outcomes and objectives by using performance Indicators.

sections.title: Alumni
sections.content: Home Alumni WELCOME ALUMINI Alumini Committee Alumni Registration Alumni Directory Association Reunions Wall of Fame Contact Us The alumni of TKRCET established in 2008 and registered under ID 322/2008 T he alumni of TKRCET, established in 2008 and registered under ID 322/2008, have quickly proven themselves to be capable engineers, scientists, and professionals. Their achievements have helped establish a positive image for their alma mater as a distinguished educational institution. Upon graduating from TKRCET, students embark on their professional journeys, where higher education plays a crucial role in their career development. Our alumni have consistently demonstrated excellence from the outset, maintaining personal connections with one another that go beyond the formal channels of the Alumni Association. For TKRCET, a special bond is formed when students complete their studies and move forward into their careers. Witnessing our graduates excel and make significant contributions in their fields fills us with immense pride and joy—an indescribable feeling that reflects the strength and spirit of our institution. REVON UNMANNED SYSTEMS PVT.LTD INAGURATION
